chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Mahlabi reported to me from Ali ibn Abdullah al-Isfahani, who reported from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who reported from Yusuf ibn Sa'id al-Arhabi, who reported from Ubaidullah ibn Musa al-Absi, from Kamil, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said:

When the people entered the house for the consultation, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi - may Allah bless him with mercy - came and said: "Allow me in with you, for I have sincere counsel for the sake of Allah and something good for you." They refused. Then he said: "Allow my head in and listen to me." They refused him even that. Then he said: "Since you refuse, then do not swear allegiance to a man who did not witness Badr, nor pledge the allegiance of al-Ridwan, and who fled on the day of Uhud when the two groups met."

Uthman said: "By Allah, if authority is given to me, I shall certainly send you back to your first Lord." When death came upon al-Miqdad, he said: "Inform Uthman that I have indeed been returned to my Lord, the First and the Last."

When the news of his death reached Uthman, he came and stood at his grave and said: "May Allah bless you with mercy; you were good, even though you were (my opponent)." He praised him well. Al-Zubair said to him: "You will know me after death when you lament me, while during my lifetime you did not provide me my sustenance." He said: "O Zubair, you say this? Do you think I like to see such a companion of Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny, die while he is resentful against me?!"

key_terms.أحد: Battle of Uhud (second major Islamic battle)
key_terms.بدر: Battle of Badr (first major Islamic battle)
key_terms.بيعة الرضوان: Pledge of al-Ridwan (Bay'at under the tree)

ai.seo_question: What did al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad say to the Shura council about the qualifications for the caliphate?
ai.summary: Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad attempted to advise the Shura council not to pledge allegiance to anyone who missed Badr, was absent from Bay'at al-Ridwan, and fled at Uhud. Uthman threatened him, but on his deathbed al-Miqdad responded defiantly. When Uthman visited his grave and praised him, al-Zubair reminded Uthman of his hypocrisy.
